question: A patient was diagnosed with Colorectal Carcinoma few months ago with metastasis and a high level of CEA. The Level of CEA in cancer will be helpful in?
explanation: CEA (Carcinoembryonic Antigen) is a tumor marker. While it may be high at the time of diagnosis, its levels are generally not used for initial staging or grading. Its most important clinical use is in post-operative surveillance (follow-up). A rising CEA level after successful surgery strongly suggests tumor recurrence or metastasis, prompting further investigation.
